item.title: The Real Story of St. Patrick: History, Faith, and the Myths
item.description:
Every year on March 17, people around the world celebrate Saint Patrick with parades, green clothing, and symbols like shamrocks. Yet the real story of the man behind the celebration is far more compelling than the legends that surround him.

Much of what we know about him comes from two short writings attributed to him: Confessio (his spiritual autobiography) and Letter to Coroticus — a rare first-person account of a missionary’s life in the early medieval Christian world.

item.title: Hula Dance & Salesforce
item.description:
Hula is a Hawaiian dance form accompanied by chant (oli) or song (mele). Developed in the Hawaiian Islands by the Native Hawaiians who originally settled there, hula dramatizes and portrays the words of the oli or mele in visual form — an excellent way of narration through movement.

Two Main Categories

Hula Kahiko (Ancient form) — accompanied by chants and traditional instruments.

Hula Auana (Contemporary form) — accompanied by western-influenced musical instruments, majorly the ukulele.

item.title: Indian Motorcycle — America's First Motorcycle Company
item.description:
TL;DR — Indian Motorcycles are not from India. They’re named after the American Indian.

The Beginning

In 1897, industry pioneer George M. Hendee founded a bicycle production company called the Hendee Manufacturing Company. Along with co-founder and chief engineer Oscar Hedstrom, Hendee opened the company’s first factory in downtown Springfield, Massachusetts in 1901.

What followed was half a century of unparalleled growth in motorcycle production and innovation, and foundational leadership in curating a true American riding culture.
